plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Ume blooms on bare branches in the cold, with fragrant blossoms in white, pink and deep red. Some trees have single flowers and others have ruffled double ones. Its scent drifts through winter gardens and orchards weeks before the cherry blossoms. In Japan it is a symbol of perseverance and the first hint of spring.
plants.location: Japan, especially mild regions of Honshu, and the Yangtze River region of China
plants.funFact: Ume is a close relative of the cherry but blooms about six weeks earlier. Its petals are rounded, while sakura petals have a notched tip.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Camellia japonica is a glossy evergreen shrub that flowers in the dull days of winter. Its rose-like blooms open in layers of satin petals around a boss of golden stamens. Gardeners prize the huge range of cultivars, from simple single cups to tightly formed doubles.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter to early spring, with many cultivars at their peak in February
plants.location: Southeastern United States, such as South Carolina, and its native range in Japan, Korea and eastern Asia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a cousin of Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: Snowdrops push through frosty ground with nodding, teardrop-shaped white flowers. Each bloom has a small green mark on its inner petals. They often appear in drifts under bare trees and are one of the first flowers of the year. Their flowers are a sign that spring is approaching.
plants.bloomingSeason: January to March, often peaking in February
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across the United Kingdom and Europe
plants.funFact: Snowdrops can bloom while snow is still on the ground. They make their own antifreeze-like proteins and can even generate a little heat to melt their way up through frost.
